learning_objective: 🎯 Let us discover the action heroes (Main Verbs) and their loyal sidekicks (Helping Verbs)!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Main verbs are the big action words (jump, run, eat). Helping verbs (is, am, are, has, do) are the friendly sidekicks that help the main verb tell the exact time of the action!
Some action words need an object to make sense. If I say 'I kicked', you will ask 'Kicked what?'. I kicked the ball! 'Kicked' is a transitive verb.
These action words are independent! They make perfect sense without needing an object. Example: 'The baby sleeps' or 'The sun shines'.

fun_activity.title: 🦸‍♂️ Action Charades
fun_activity.instructions: Act out a main verb (like swimming or eating) without talking. Ask your siblings to guess the verb!

quick_recap: ⭐ Main verbs show the actual action, while helping verbs support them.
⭐ Words like 'has', 'have', 'do', and 'does' are very common helping verbs.
⭐ Transitive verbs need an object to be complete, but intransitive verbs do not.
